# F4

> F4 is a free, open-source sticker app for macOS, like WhatsApp stickers but for the whole Mac: a Spotlight-like floating panel that searches a local library of stickers (PNG, WebP, GIF, JPEG, animated ones included) and copies one to the clipboard in a keystroke, ready to paste in WhatsApp, Slack, Telegram or any other app. Native Swift app (SwiftUI and AppKit), macOS 14 Sonoma or later, Apple Silicon and Intel, MIT license, no special permissions, no tracking, no account. The interface is English, with an Italian translation when macOS runs in Italian. Website: https://f4.kkratter.com/ (English) and https://f4.kkratter.com/it/ (Italian). FAQ: https://f4.kkratter.com/faq/

Key facts:

- The default shortcut is F4, from any app; on a Mac keyboard that means fn-F4, because the top row are media keys (Spotlight or Launchpad). The shortcut is fixed: it cannot be changed. The panel floats above everything, including full-screen apps, and has no Dock icon (the app lives in the menu bar). There is no Settings window and nothing to set: the menu bar menu opens F4, lists recent stickers, manages folders and packs, checks for updates and quits. F4 adds itself to the login items on the first launch.
- The library is one folder: F4's own, `~/Library/Application Support/F4/Memes`, by default. F4 watches it with FSEvents, so new files appear without a restart. Subfolders become categories you can search, each top-level folder is a tab in the panel, managed from the panel (⌘K actions on the selected sticker, ⌘M move to a folder, ⌘R rename, ⌘T tags, ⌘⌫ trash, or right-click) and from the menu bar (Folders).
- Add stickers by pasting: copy any sticker or image, press fn F4, press ⌘V (WhatsApp/Telegram: right-click a sticker → Copy). A pasted image is named after its caption, or what it shows, read on the Mac with Vision. A photo or meme becomes a 512×512 sticker (the whole picture fitted in the square, the rest transparent); transparent PNGs, GIFs and WebP are kept as they are, and ⌥⌘V keeps any picture as it is. The first launch shows these steps. Links and files work too: files can be dropped on the panel, and Add opens a file picker. A WhatsApp sticker pack (`.wastickers`) can be dropped, pasted, added or opened from a link: F4 unpacks it into a folder named after the pack. The menu bar's Packs switches ready-made packs on (downloaded into the library, only then) and off.
- Supported files: PNG, WebP (animated too), GIF and JPEG, plus `.wastickers` packs. HEIC and short videos are planned.
- Type to search (fuzzy, on file names, folder names and Finder tags), arrow keys to move in the grid, Tab or ⌘1…⌘9 to switch between the Stickers, Favourites and folder tabs, Enter to copy (or drag a sticker out of the panel into another app), Escape to close. Favourites (the star on a sticker, or ⌘D) come first, then recently copied stickers.
- Copying writes the file URL (`public.file-url`) and the raw file bytes under the file's UTI, never a decoded `NSImage`, so animated stickers stay animated when pasted.
- A starter pack is built in, so the panel is never empty: animated emoji (Google Noto Animated Emoji, CC BY 4.0) and stickers F4 draws in code ("basito", "dai dai dai", "ship it", the F4 keycap...) and a folder of meme cats (`maramao/`), each folder copied once into F4's own library (`Emoji/`, `F4/`, `maramao/`) as ordinary files (a folder added in an update arrives on the next launch); with a folder of the user's own (picked in an older version) they are listed after the user's stickers instead, and Show Starter Pack in the menu bar menu hides them.
- After a copy a "Copied to Clipboard" toast appears at the bottom of the screen; the user pastes with Command-V. F4 needs no permission at all: the global shortcut uses Carbon `RegisterEventHotKey`.
- The empty state draws the "F4, basito" face from the Italian series Boris in code; a `.basito.png`, `.gif` or `.jpg` in the sticker folder replaces it. Typing some Boris or The Office lines, or the Konami code, in the search field triggers easter eggs.
- Scripts, Shortcuts and AI agents drive it with URLs: `f4://open`, `f4://search?q=…` (panel with the search typed in), `f4://copy?name=…` (copies the best match without showing the panel, e.g. `open "f4://copy?name=basito"`), `f4://reload`, `f4://settings` (opens the menu bar menu).
- F4 goes online only to check for updates with Sparkle (the appcast on this site; can be turned off), to download links the user pastes or drops, and to download packs the user switches on: no analytics, no account, no server.

## Install

- Download the latest DMG from https://github.com/kkratterf/f4/releases/latest/download/F4.dmg and drag F4 to Applications.
- Or one line in Terminal: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kkratterf/f4/main/install.sh | sh`
- Or Homebrew: `brew tap kkratterf/f4 https://github.com/kkratterf/f4 && brew install --cask f4`
- The app is not notarized by Apple yet. If macOS blocks the first launch, open System Settings > Privacy & Security and click "Open Anyway" next to the F4 message, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/F4.app`. The install script does this for you.
- Uninstall: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kkratterf/f4/main/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall`, or `brew uninstall --zap --cask f4`.

## Optional

- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/kkratterf/f4/blob/main/AGENTS.md): for agents that change F4. The code map, build and test, CI, the rules a change must respect, commit and PR format, how a release is cut. Written for AI agents and humans alike.
